Subject: MSA + private deployment addendum — initial redlines

Marcus,

Thanks for the call earlier. Attaching our redline of the MSA and a short exhibit describing the evidence and operator access we’d expect for an on-prem / VPC deployment. High-level asks:

- License scope: explicit right to run the model in our VPC for our internal patient data workloads (no sublicensing).
- Snapshot/escrow-like access: mechanism for us to obtain a read-only snapshot of binaries + run instructions if Redwood becomes unavailable for >60 days.
- Audit evidence: targeted SOC2 artifacts, runbook excerpts, and a one-time test window for our auditors.

Attached: Caduceus_MSA_Redlines_20261101.docx (redlines), plus a short exhibit in the workbook.

Can you confirm who at Redwood will own the legal coordination and whether you can provide a draft addendum in the next 5 business days? We like to align procurement and security windows so our audit team can sign off before year-end.

Thanks,

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 11:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MSA + private deployment addendum — initial redlines

Alicia / Marcus,

Thanks for the redlines. I reviewed the MSA and the exhibit. High-level notes before we draft formal language:

- License scope: we can accept a customer-limited license to run in their VPC for the specified internal workloads. We will need a carve-out preserving Redwood’s right to provide model updates and to run Redwood-hosted diagnostic tools for support (we can limit telemetry).

- Snapshot/escrow: instead of an escrow of binaries, Redwood proposes a "contingent access" path:
  a) A certified snapshot (read-only) of model weights + container images encrypted to a customer-managed key, stored with a neutral custodian;
  b) Access is triggered only after an agreed set of conditions (material failure to support > 60 days OR insolvency);
  c) Access includes transfer instructions, a checksum manifest, and a one-week support window from Redwood engineers to help validate.

- Audit evidence: we can provide SOC2 artifact extracts, runbook snippets, and a single four-hour auditor test window in the staging environment. We cannot provide production DB exports or customer data.

Open questions we will propose language for in the addendum:
1) Precise trigger definition for access (what constitutes "unavailable").
2) Custodian selection and cost allocation.
3) Acceptance criteria for the snapshot (format, encryption algorithm, transfer tooling).

I’ll circulate a draft addendum and the exhibit language tomorrow. If Caduceus prefers a different snapshot path (e.g., on-demand read-only API escrow) let us know so we can include it as an alternative.

Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com

From: Ben Cho <ben.cho@caduceus.health>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Alicia Torres <alicia.torres@caduceus.health>, contracts@caduceus.health
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 10:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MSA + private deployment addendum — initial redlines

Lauren, Marcus,

Thanks for the quick review and the proposed contingency approach. A few clarifications from the security team:

- Trigger: our preference is a 60-day service interruption OR failure to meet mutually-agreed throughput/latency SLAs for two consecutive weeks. We understand Redwood's request to limit triggers and are open to narrow SLA-based triggers.

- Custodian: neutral custodian is preferred. We will share a short list; cost can be split 50/50 for the first year.

- Snapshot format: we can accept an encrypted container image + manifest. We need a signature from Redwood to verify integrity, and a small verification script (bash/python) for our auditors.

Also attaching a short spreadsheet mapping the security questions to the artifacts we need (Caduceus_Security_Questions.xlsx). Can you confirm Redwood can provide the verification script as part of the transfer package?

Best,
Ben Cho
Security Architect
Caduceus Health

Attachment: Caduceus_Security_Questions.xlsx

Folks,

Great alignment so far. Quick summary and next steps:

- Redwood will deliver a draft addendum (license + snapshot exhibit + custodian path) by EOD Monday 2026-11-08. Lauren will own the legal text.
- Technical deliverables: Marissa will coordinate with your security team to validate the manifest format and the verification script; Redwood engineering will produce the verification script as part of the transfer package (we’ll provide a small support window to walk auditors through verification).
- Trigger: we will propose the hybrid trigger (60-day unavailability OR SLA degradation window). We will add concrete SLA language for throughput/latency metrics in the exhibit.
- Custodian: Marcus to share Redwood’s preferred neutral custodian options; procurement can comment on cost split.

Marissa will reach out now to schedule the security sync for next week. If Caduceus can confirm preferred times, we’ll lock the slot.
